title: Responsibilities and data flows
lesson: The app processes metadata and personal organisation. The music stream and WiiM control are outside its Dart code.

title: Domain models in memory
lesson: Objects, domain relationships and SQL tables are different views. Of particular importance: categories store IDs, and album tracks exist only in the detail page state.

title: Session management and testability
lesson: The store, clock and HTTP client are interchangeable. Expiry times, storage failures and concurrent requests can therefore be tested without real TIDAL access.

title: Artist editor: input, draft and storage
lesson: The draft separates provisional input from the stored state. A Dart extension is not inheritance and therefore has no generalisation arrow.

title: User interface: objects and callbacks
lesson: Widgets receive data and functions through constructors. A callback can trigger a reload of the parent view after saving.

title: App startup: cache and stored session
lesson: Two asynchronous tasks start together. A loaded cache is displayed independently of the completion of a later network update; tokens and albums are read separately.

title: Interactive sign-in and secure storage
lesson: Successful sign-in and successful persistent storage are two different results. This distinction prevents false promises about the next app startup.

title: Loading the library: foreground and background
lesson: During background synchronisation, the old view is retained until the complete new state is available. Foreground loading, by contrast, displays subsets that have already been read.

title: From JSON resources to Album objects
lesson: Collection IDs and album metadata come from separate requests. The resource index resolves the relationships to artists and covers.

title: API 401: refresh once and retry
lesson: A network error is not evidence of an invalid sign-in. Concurrent calls share the refresh; a second rejection ends without an infinite loop.

title: Editing and saving sort names in bulk
lesson: No saving on every keystroke: a confirmed change list is written together. The page knows only its save callback, not the specific SQL.

title: Assigning an album to several categories
lesson: The checkboxes return only IDs. The detail page then initiates the transaction and reports the change to parent pages.

title: Cover display: file, download and fallback
lesson: A File is not an album record. The UI receives a file or null; cover requests do not use an OAuth Bearer header.

title: Loading album details and handing off to TIDAL
lesson: The track list and categories come from different sources. An external link hands off to another app and is not a music player implemented here.
